diagram_math_checks.justification: All stages have N=rs complex coordinates. Input x is in C^N; splitting gives r vectors x^(u) in C^s. A has indices (u,k2) in {0,...,r-1} x {0,...,s-1}; y is equivalently s vectors of length r; z has indices (k1,k2) in the same product size. Ranges are stated immediately above the figure, matching Statement and F2.
j=u+rv is the bijective input index map in F2 and proof step 1.1; x^(u)_v=x_(u+rv) is exactly the Statement definition. No coprimality is introduced.
For each fixed u, F_s:C^s -> C^s yields A_(u,k2)=(F_s x^(u))(k2). There are r transforms, with negative exponent -2*pi*i*v*k2/s and factor s^(-1/2) from local DFT supplier Definition/F1 and step 3.1.

Coordinatewise multiplication sends A_(u,k2) to y_u^(k2)=exp(-2*pi*i*u*k2/N) A_(u,k2), exactly the Statement and the exponent decomposition in step 2.1. The sign is explicitly negative, and neither coordinate changes.

For each fixed k2, F_r:C^r -> C^r gives z_(k1,k2)=(F_r y^(k2))(k1); there are s such transforms. Step 3.1 proves the displayed equality with (F_N x)(k2+s*k1). F2 gives the output bijection. Product normalization s^(-1/2)r^(-1/2)=N^(-1/2) follows from step 2.1/F4.

The native figure visibly has five stage boxes and four downward arrows in the order split, F_s, twiddle, F_r. It asserts a sequential factorization, not a cyclic graph or an extra commutative square. No crossings, graph-closing edge, or open/closed scalar endpoints are applicable.
